newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine finance ministry delays T-bill payments.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine finance ministry delays T-bill payments.

text.p: Ukraine's finance ministry has failed to pay 3.9 trillion karbovanets ($22 million) in interest and principal on Treasury bills due on Thursday morning, bankers said on Thursday.
As of midday local time a maturing three-month T-bill had not been paid, and quarterly interest on a nine-month and a 12-month issue had not been paid, they said.
A finance ministry official in charge of internal debt told Reuters that the ministry would not provide information on the matter and could not say why the money was still unpaid.

A spokesman in the central bank's capital markets department said the ministry had not properly calculated the amount of money necessary to meet the payments, and had also not informed the central bank when the payments would be made.

Ukraine is withdrawing the karbovanets currency from circulation by September 16 and replacing it with the hryvnia, but calculations on T-bill transactions are still being conducted in the old currency.
The hryvnia was unchanged at 1.76 to the dollar on the Ukraine Interbank Currency Exchange on Thursday. One hryvnia equals 100,000 karbovanets.
Bankers gave various reasons for non-payment.
TK-Kredit bank trader Serhiy Krushevsky said the finance ministry did not have the money to pay.
"The ministry is starting to make a practice of delaying payments," he said.

In late August payments were delayed half a day, and finance ministry officials blamed commercial banks for being late in paying for T-bills bought earlier in the week, which in turn delayed the ministry making its payments.
Alexander Okhrymenko of Bank Ukraina said the payments were being delayed because of infighting between the ministry and central bank.
"There is disagreement between the central bank and the Finance Ministry over who should establish yields at auctions," he said.
Igor Frunze of Finance and Credit bank said banks were losing confidence in the ministry.
Officials at the state savings bank Oshchadbank, a major buyer of T-bills, said there was no reason for panic and the money would be paid soon.
Finance ministry officials have said previously that there have been several delays since Ukraine started its T-bill market 18 months ago.
The ministry is due to pay 779.9 billion on September 13, 4.1 trillion karbovanets on September 18 and 8.3 trillion karbovanets on September 25.

The central bank plans to raise 150 billion karbovanets this year in T-bill sales to go towards covering the projected 467 trillion karbovanets budget deficit. --Natalya Zinets, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 229 2264
